body:
> Anyway, fingers crossed that I haven't wasted your time by misreading the code :)

No worries. Thank you for taking the time to file this thoughtful GitHub issue!

> so we might hope that those keys are guaranteed to be unique. If that was the whole story, I think it would still be worth a comment in the code. ("NB: The following is only valid because we're hashing the keys of a map. Do not copy this approach if you can't guarantee the inputs are all distinct.")

Commit [95704d1](https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/commit/95704d1e0b1ba853548984afc171ab14a475bf50) refactored some of the helper methods out of `DigestUtils.java` and into the new `MetadataDigestUtils.java`. `DigestUtils.java` wisely had a comment to this effect ([here](https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/blob/f0e63c4c934dfd9e85d2e55ede7c5bc0409946c7/src/main/java/com/google/devtools/build/lib/vfs/DigestUtils.java#L32-L38)) but that commit didn't move/copy the comment. This seems like an oversight to me; I agree it'd be nice to have a code comment documenting to code readers that the fishy behavior is not a blatant bug. We should add one.

> (Similarly, the fromMetadata method immediately above that one.) ... One detail that jumps out to me is that hashing appears to be done by encoding each string into Protobuf bytes. That entails a conversion from Java's UTF-16 strings to Protobuf's UTF-8 strings

The `fromMetadata` operates on pairs where the first element is a path string. These path strings are not arbitrary UTF-16; they are latin1 byte arrays slapped into a `java.lang.String` as-is: notice how `bazel/src/main/native/unix_jni.cc` consistently operates in latin1-land. (There's an open work item against me / my team to document this more clearly in the codebase.) So I don't think your concern applies.

If I'm right, then you concern applies theoretically to only the `fromEnv` method. There I imagine the next question is the source of those strings.

`fromEnv` is only used to compute a digest of the client environment for purposes of the action cache. We could easily change that to use a sorted map, but changing the digest function would result in the action cache having mismatches across bazel versions. It would be easy to keep the same digest for the common case of an empty map, but if the map is non-empty the user could see confusing messages that the client env has changed when in fact it hasn't: http://google3/third_party/bazel/src/main/java/com/google/devtools/build/lib/actions/ActionCacheChecker.java;l=238;rcl=461281665.

A compromise could be to move `fromEnv` out of a common place to discourage any new uses.
I'm happy to approve a fix. The easiest thing to do seems like sorting, so long as there is no performance concern. Did you have anything else in mind?

issue.title: Use `+` instead of `^` to combine digests

repository.name: bazel
repository.description: a fast, scalable, multi-language and extensible build system

issue.body:
Use + as in Guava's Hashing.combineUnordered. This has a number of advantages over XOR, which was used in the past:
* Identical inputs will not cancel each other out.
* Due to the carry, addition isn't a linear operation on the level of bit vectors. This prevents adversaries from producing linear combinations (i.e., subsets of input sets) that collide with other inputs.

Also removes an unused test helper.

Fixes #15660

body: I went with `+` instead of `^`, which is used by both Guava and the JDK's `Set` `hashCode`. It avoids the pressing problems while being as fast as `^`.
